fixed.problem: Blocking 1: after a restart, a status write that had waited for GitHub was sent only when a screen read the status words or the runner sent a new event, because nothing called StatusBoard.resumeAll. If a person quit while GitHub was unreachable, their comment kept a stale Working on now line. Quit's clearing had no test. Sibling found: every close cleared the shared record's Working on now lines and wrote the comment without them, including a CLI one-shot's close (an fr command composed beside a running daemon), while the daemon's task was still running.
fixed.failing_test_before: apps/ui/test/two-installs.test.ts "memory: Quit while a task runs and GitHub does not answer: at the next start, with GitHub back and no screen open, the comment loses its Working on now line, in one edit of the same comment". Before the fix it failed with 'still waiting after 60 s ... no write'. New cases beside it: the same file's "memory: Quit while a task runs with GitHub answering clears its Working on now line before the daemon ends; nothing of the writer runs after, and the next start writes nothing", and packages/runtime/test/status-board.test.ts's "fixup-w8-status-write: Quit clears a running task's Working on now line ...; after the close no event and no timer writes", "... a one-shot's close ... leaves the daemon's Working on now line" and "... the start sends what waited with no screen asking; GitHub still out at the start, the retry sends it once it answers, once".
fixed.how: compose now calls statusBoard.resumeAll() at start, after the device row is registered. It does so when the board is wired and the runtime is the install's daemon: the new ComposeOptions.statusDaemon, which defaults to recoverSessions and so to the daemon. If GitHub is still out at the start, the board's 60 s retry timer sends the text later. StatusBoard.close takes { withinMs, clearWorking }. compose passes clearWorking: statusDaemon, so a one-shot leaves the daemon's lines alone in the record and on GitHub. resumeAll does nothing after close. The two-home harness (apps/ui/test/two-installs.ts) gains home.quit() and home.start() as appended helpers. quit() sends POST /shutdown as the desktop shell sends it, then closes the runtime as fr daemon does; start() composes the home again. The homes compose with statusDaemon: true.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Bench (done, /tmp/frbench/fixup-w8-status-write/steps/rewalk-restart-result.json). Cut Bob's GitHub, run a session for a new task, restart his daemon while GitHub is still cut, turn GitHub back on, and open no screen. After 60 s the stand-in logged 'PATCH /repos/team/shared/issues/comments/1022' and 'PATCH /repos/team/shared/issues/2' from bob. Live check on real GitHub: (1) Start a task in a repository project and wait until your comment on the status issue shows 'Working on now' with the task's title. (2) Turn the network off and Quit Forerunner. (3) Turn the network on and start Forerunner, opening no Settings or Docs. (4) Within about a minute the same comment (same id, shown as edited) loses its Working on now line, and no second comment appears. (5) Repeat with the network on at Quit: the line is gone from the comment before the app has closed.

fixed.problem: Blocking 3 (W8a-left-3): a token that lost access to a private repository gets 404 on every call, and the board read any 404 as 'GitHub did not answer'. Settings and the Docs tab then promised 'it updates when GitHub answers', and the update never came; a 60 s timer retried forever. A comment deleted between the read and the edit waited for the next event instead of being written again.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/status-board.test.ts "W8a-left-3: a token that lost access answers 404 (every call, or only the edit while reads work): one issue, no new comment, the no-permission sentence, and no retry on a timer" (the place was 'waiting') and "W8a-left-3: the comment deleted between the read and the edit (the edit answers 404, the issue reads): exactly one comment is written again, and no second issue" (no comment was written).
fixed.how: In write()'s catch, a 'missing' refusal now goes to whyMissing, which reads again with the same host. If the repository is no longer readable, or everything still reads but the write was refused, the place is no_permission: the sentence is 'Status stays in the app: Forerunner may not write issues on team/shared (the GitHub key needs Issues: read and write).' and no retry timer is set; the next task, session or screen tries again. If the stored issue or this writer's comment is gone, there is exactly one more write at once (again: true). That write recreates the comment, and W8-write-8's rule handles a deleted issue. If a re-read gets no answer, the text keeps waiting as before. getIssueComment answering null counts as a 404. An edit that answered 404 never opens a second issue or comment.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Live check: in a private repository project, run one session so your comment exists. Then remove the GitHub key's access to that repository (or revoke the repository from a fine-grained token) and run another session. Settings > Advanced > Other settings > Status issue on GitHub reads 'Status stays in the app: Forerunner may not write issues on <owner/repo> (the GitHub key needs Issues: read and write).', and it does not read 'it updates when GitHub answers'. GitHub shows no new issue or comment. Give the access back and run a session: the same comment is edited in place.

new_problems: The status board's Quit clear relies on the close; when the session's end reaches the board first (the usual case), sessionEnded already clears the lines. A write in flight past close's 5 s window can still finish after the store closes (an HTTP call that hangs rather than refuses); fr daemon exits right after, so only tests could see it.

The two-person bench's restart re-walk session for a new task ended in about a second with no task done (Bob's comment's Last session reads 'finished no task'), as the reviewer also saw; the status path was exercised, but that task did not run.
notes_for_other_areas: ComposeOptions.statusDaemon (default recoverSessions, so the daemon): only the install's daemon resumes waiting status texts at start (StatusBoard.resumeAll) and clears Working on now at Quit. StatusBoard.close({ clearWorking: false }) is a one-shot's close. A test that composes a daemon with startServices: false passes statusDaemon: true (the two-home harness does).

Two-home harness (apps/ui/test/two-installs.ts), appended helpers: home.quit() sends POST /shutdown as the desktop shell's Quit, lets holds go, settles and closes the runtime, and leaves the home stopped; home.start() composes it again. two.close() skips a stopped home.

StatusBoard write: a 404 ('missing') is read again (whyMissing). The repository not readable, or everything readable while the write was refused, means place no_permission with no retry timer; the stored issue or this writer's comment gone means one more write at once. w8-status-read can rely on place no_permission for lost access.
